p.i: ab aliis perfectam glaciem. Nam ut natura comparatum est res non nasci simul & perfici, nec in lucem omnia prodire, non ita primi singulas res librarunt, aut libarunt, ut posteris omnem scribendi praripuerint facultatem. Verum iniuriam me tanti viri fama facere putarem, si ex uno opere, ut [?]ἐκ φῆς ὀνύχων τὸν λέοντα, ingenii magnitudinem existimarem. Dicam vere, & ut mos meus liberè, eum ἀπὸ τὸ μήνιγγα [?]τῷ ἐγχε-φάλῳ, quod de Jove fabulantur, tot edidisse Palladas, easq; adversus malum liuoris dentem armatas, quot libros conscripsit. In ea vero ætatis asta-[?]te, qua in publicum literarum theatrum productus floret, neq; octavum agonem Olympicum numeravit, tam uberes protulit ingenii fructus, ut ipsis

page.notes: The first word of the printed "glaciem" appears as "glaciem" in print; left as printed. Greek passages are only partly legible: the first Greek phrase (ἐκ φῆς ὀνύχων) and the second Greek phrase (before ἐγχε-φάλῳ) are doubtful and marked [?]. "ætatis asta-te" at the line end: the hyphenated word is doubtful. "Ioue" changed to "Jove" as a consonant. "ingenij" changed to "ingenii" as a vowel i. "eafq;" changed to "easq;". "octauum" changed to "octavum" as a consonant v. Long s rendered as plain s throughout. The text ends mid-sentence on "ipsis" and continues on the next page.
